answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce bond before claiming rewards, then slash it when audits prove fraud. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate bond for every fake account; splitting one stake among many identities will not meet the minimum. Random audits can trace claims through a shared vertex, raising the chance of exposure. The attacker pays in locked capital and forfeited bonds, while honest agents recover theirs, even across an ocean of accounts. The copper cost is real, not merely a registration fee.
